messages.subject: Hutton's shearwater carcass density
parts:
This is a multi-part message in MIME format.

------=_NextPart_000_00C8_01BFA9EF.28908120
Content-Type: text/plain;
charset="iso-8859-9"
Content-Transfer-Encoding: quoted-printable

Gudday,
I'm currently performing data analysis in DISTANCE aiming to estimate =
the density of Hutton's shearwater carcasses on the ground within their =
major breeding colony. Hutton's shearwater is an endangered New =
Zealand-endemic petrel whose breeding range has contracted to two =
localized sites in the Seaward Kaikoura Mountains. We are trying to =
figure out whether predation by stoats is a cause for concern about the =
viability of the two remaining colonies. =20

I'm quite new to Distance Sampling, but feel that I've grasped the basic =
concepts and am fairly happy using the software. However, before I =
submit my report to the NZ Department of Conservation I'd really like to =
go over what I've done with a DISTANCE veteran. My data set is quite =
small and simple, so I imagine that this will take only a short time. =
To demonstrate this I include a summary of the output I have obtained =
below. My main concern is that I've missed some way of obtaining more =
precise estimates than those presented in the table.

Year
N
D
L 95% CI
U 95% CI
=20
1996
22
14.70
9.45
22.87
=20
1997
27
13.41
8.95
20.10
=20
1998
22
13.14
8.45
20.45
=20
1999
47
11.37
8.24
15.694
=20
Pooled
118
12.66
10.42
15.400
=20

I'd be most grateful if anyone feels like sparing some minutes for this =
very worthwhile conservation project. I'll be happy to tell more about =
the bird if requested.

Yours sincerely
Josh Kemp

c/-Department of Conservation
Nelson
New Zealand

Ph 64 3 546 3291
email; josh...@ihug.co.nz
